sectionsUsed: 5.1 Table Basics: a table consists of rows and columns; the number and order of columns is fixed and each column has a name
5.5.4 Primary Keys: values must be both unique and not null (o1)

5.5.5 Foreign Keys: values must match a row of the referenced table, referential integrity; a table can have more than one foreign key to implement many-to-many relationships, with the order_items example (o2, o3)
5.5.5: a referencing row is exempt from the foreign key check when its referencing column is null; declare NOT NULL to require a match (o2 first definition, recap, cheat sheet)
5.5.5: default ON DELETE NO ACTION, so deleting a referenced row raises an error; RESTRICT and CASCADE options (o2, cheat sheet)
3.3 Foreign Keys: inserting a row that references a missing parent is rejected with an error
